mainEntity.name: How much does a Vauxhall Insignia 2.0 CDTI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Vauxhall Insignia 2.0 CDTI engine replacement typically costs £1,600-£3,300 for a reconditioned or rebuilt unit supply-only, with fitting adding £600-£1,200 depending on the workshop. Used engines: £500-£2,000 depending on code and mileage. Reconditioned: £1,600-£2,800. Rebuilt: £1,800-£3,300. Full supply & fit: £2,200-£4,500 total.

mainEntity.name: What is the most common failure on the Vauxhall Insignia 2.0 CDTI engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most documented and critical failure is the oil pump seal failure, which causes oil pressure loss and catastrophic crankshaft bearing damage. This typically occurs around 125,000 miles. Other common issues include timing chain tensioner wear, EGR valve clogging and DPF regeneration failure. If you notice the oil pressure warning light or hear knocking, stop driving immediately.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Vauxhall Insignia 2.0 CDTI?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's value and condition. A typical Insignia 2.0 CDTI (2008-2017) is worth £1,500-£5,000. If the car is worth under £2,500 and needs a full engine replacement, scrap value may be the better option. If the car is worth £3,000+, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine (£1,600-£3,300) is usually financially viable. If the oil pump seal has failed but the engine block is intact, a seal replacement (£500-£900) is often the most cost-effective solution.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Vauxhall Insignia 2.0 CDTI engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical Vauxhall Insignia 2.0 CDTI engine replacement takes 1-3 days for a specialist workshop. Oil pump seal replacement: 6-10 hours labour. Timing chain replacement: 8-12 hours labour. Full engine swap: 12-18 hours depending on engine code, transmission type and 4WD system. Supply & fit lead time: 3-7 working days from quote acceptance to completion.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between A20DTH and B20DTH in the Insignia 2.0 CDTI?

acceptedAnswer.text: These are different generations of the same 2.0 CDTI engine family. A20DTH: 160hp - found in Insignia Mk1 (2008-2017); most common and most failure-prone variant. B20DTH: 170hp - found in later Mk1 (2015-2017) and Mk2 (2017-2022); Euro 6 compliant with AdBlue system. Both share the oil pump seal vulnerability, though B20DTH has some revisions. Enter your registration above to confirm which code is fitted to your Insignia.

mainEntity.name: Does a replacement Vauxhall Insignia 2.0 CDTI engine come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - every rebuilt and reconditioned Vauxhall Insignia 2.0 CDTI engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Warranty covers manufacturing defects and component failure. Upgraded oil pump seal and timing chain components are fitted to prevent the original failures. historyTimeline.h2: Vauxhall Insignia 2.0 CDTI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Vauxhall Insignia 2.0 CDTI, powered by the GM Family II diesel engine, was introduced with the Insignia's launch in 2008 and continued through both the Mk1 (A) and Mk2 (B) generations until 2022. It became the backbone of the Insignia range, prized for its torque and motorway economy, but also notorious for a critical oil pump seal and crankshaft design flaw that can cause catastrophic failure.

milestones.description: Insignia Mk1 (A) launched; A20DT (130hp) and A20DTH (160hp) 2.0 CDTI variants introduced
2017 - A20DTC (110hp), A20DTL (110hp), A20DTJ (131hp), A20DTE (170hp) variants added across the Mk1 range
Facelift Mk1 introduced; B20DTH (170hp) replaces A20DTH in some applications
B20DTH (170hp) and B20DTF (BiTurbo) introduced with Euro 6 emissions compliance
Insignia Mk2 (B) Grand Sport and Sports Tourer launched; B20DTH (170hp) carried over
2022 - B20DTH, D20DTH and D20DTR (BiTurbo) variants used in Mk2

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Vauxhall Insignia 2.0 CDTI is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Vauxhall Insignia 2.0 CDTI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Vauxhall Insignia 2.0 CDTI is a capable motorway cruiser with strong torque and fuel economy, but it is defined by one critical design flaw: the oil pump seal. The A20DTH and A20DTE codes dominate replacement demand for the Insignia 2.0 CDTI. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Oil Pump Seal Failure - The Insignia 2.0 CDTI's Achilles' Heel
problems.rootCause: A poorly designed oil pump seal in the sump fails, causing a loss of oil pressure. The oil pressure warning light often illuminates too late - by then, the crankshaft bearings have already started to spin, grinding themselves to destruction. This is not an isolated incident; it is a disturbingly common occurrence across the 2.0 CDTI family. The failure is often catastrophic and irreparable.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New oil pump seal and oil pickup pipe; sump drop and reseal
repairOptions.longevity: Best value if caught before bearing damage; 100k-120k mile preventative measure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When bearings have spun causing crankshaft damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Vauxhall Insignia 2.0 CDTI (2008-2017) sits in the £1,500-£5,000 range depending on mileage, trim and condition. For vehicles worth under £2,500, a full engine replacement may approach or exceed the vehicle's value. A preventative oil pump seal replacement (£500-£900) is excellent value if caught early. For vehicles worth £3,000+, a reconditioned engine is usually financially viable if the car is otherwise sound.
problems.recommendation: If your Insignia 2.0 CDTI is approaching 100,000 miles, have the oil pump seal inspected or replaced preventatively. This is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement and addresses the root cause. If you hear knocking or see the oil pressure warning light, stop driving immediately - continued operation will destroy the engine. If the engine has already suffered catastrophic failure, a rebuilt or reconditioned unit through EnginesMarket is the cost-effective route - warranty included.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Rattle on Start-Up
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner can wear, allowing the chain to rattle on cold start. If ignored, the chain can skip or snap, causing valve and piston damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full chain kit with tensioner, guides and gears
repairOptions.longevity: Best value if caught early; prevents catastrophic failure

problems.h4: EGR Valve & DPF System Clogging - Emissions System Failures
problems.rootCause: EGR valve clogging is a common failure point, causing rough running, power loss and engine management lights. EGR faults can disable DPF regeneration. DPF blockage is common in urban-driven Insignias, with DPF soot levels reaching 137% or more.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chemical or manual cleaning of EGR valve
Forced DPF regeneration or professional cleaning

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For Insignia 2.0 CDTI examples under £2,500, EGR cleaning (£180-£350) is almost always worth trying. DPF replacement at £800-£1,500 may represent 30-60% of vehicle value - carefully evaluate the car's overall condition before proceeding.
problems.recommendation: Regular motorway driving to allow passive DPF regeneration is the best prevention. If you see the DPF warning light, follow the manual's regeneration instructions immediately. EGR faults often appear alongside DPF issues - have both inspected together to avoid repeat workshop visits.
